main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling devil curry in the shared flat without its smell affecting the others' laundry, rooms and work; A and B initially wanted it stopped.

A-B.evidence: B agrees with A's initial request (turn 2). A accepts weekends (turn 7), but B says the smell still gets into the room (turn 8), then accepts a warning so she can shut her door (turns 12, 14). They never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C backs the no-smell stance (turn 3). A settles for weekends (turn 7), but C keeps objecting about laundry and refuses to pay for a fan (turns 9, 36). A is silent after turn 7.

A-D.evidence: D initially refuses to stop cooking (turn 4). A proposes weekends in turn 5, D agrees in turn 6, and A thanks D in turn 7.

B-C.evidence: C says 'She's right' in support of B (turn 9). B later accepts D's notice plan (turn 14) while C keeps raising new objections (turns 15, 28, 36).

B-D.evidence: D offers advance notice (turn 10). B says that helps and asks for a heads-up to shut her door (turn 12). D agrees (turn 13) and B thanks D (turn 14).

C-D.evidence: D keeps offering options and C rejects each (turns 17, 28). C proposes the fan (turn 32) and D partly accepts if the cost is split (turn 33). C refuses to pay (turn 36), so the dispute remains.
